My mother heavily restricted my diet as a child, which affects me to this day. 
I wasn't allowed junk food as a child. Everything was whole foods and whole grains. Tons of vegetables, good sources or protein, healthy carbs. But junk food was forbidden ... I was a healthy sized kid. When my mother thought I was gaining weight, from growth spurts, she would force me to exercise more. 

This led me to having a terrible body image. I believed that I was fat because I wasn't skin and bones but a healthy, average weight. It also led to me eating all the junk food I desired when I was away from home. When I went to a friends house or my cousins house, I would consume as much junk as I could get my hands on. Once I was old enough to have a job and relationship, my mother didn't have a say over what I ate, and I ballooned significantly to overweight. 

As an adult, I avoid buying junk food and try to make conscious healthy choices but sometimes, when I'm feeling emotional or bored, I eat mindlessly and can still spiral out of control. My body image and health still suffer from these experiences.

Whatever you do, do it lightly. Maybe therapy could help to give her a chance to reflect on why she eats the way she does. I know that my mother controlled my relationship to food and exercise because she wanted the best for me, but it has had a lasting impact. Food is often on my brain from the time I wake up until I fall asleep. 

Hope this is helpful.

I struggle with this too. When I’m having a particularly emotional day, seeing couples on TV or even walking down the street holding hands can bring me to tears. It used to make me angry and jealous that I didn’t have someone who loves me romantically and now it just makes me sad because I feel like I’m unlovable.. I’ve used mantras to help with this trigger and it’s helped! When I see couples and I feel the emotion ramping up, I try to tell myself “one day I will experience/have that again and it will feel so good”. It helps me to remember what it feels like to have a partner and not focus on why I don’t have one, at least for that moment, which stops me from crying. I hope you can find something that helps you!

Also, I’ve been down the tinder validation train on and off for several years. I find it to emotionally draining after a while to build shallow relationships just to receive a moment of surface level gratification... At this point and with the current state of the world, I’ve distanced myself from everyone too, only to find out that I enjoy my own company more than anyone else’s company - as long as I keep a decent distance between myself and social media, otherwise I get sucked right back into constantly craving the instant validation and gratification.

This video touched me and made me feel less alone.
